reviews.author: Manuel São Bento
reviews.content:
FULL SPOILER-FREE REVIEW @ https://movieswetextedabout.com/nobody-2-movie-review-bob-odenkirk-returns-in-an-action-sequel-that-knows-its-audience/

"Nobody 2 isn't going to redefine the genre or make anyone's top-ten lists of the year, but it fulfills its mission perfectly: entertain its target audience for ninety minutes with inventive, stunt-driven action, sharp humor, and a charismatic lead.

It's one of those cases where the formula, even worn out, still works thanks to competent execution and the collective enthusiasm of cast and crew. If the formula is here to stay, so be it - just keep the smile on my face.

As long as that balance between violence and lightness remains, along with the commitment to creative, stunt-led set pieces, bring on the third one."

Rating: B

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: I must admit, I’d completely forgotten “Nobody” (2021) when I sat down to watch this, but once it picks up an head of steam it’s actually quite a good fun, entirely senseless, stream of violence that does raise a smile. Still beholden to “The Barber” (Colin Salmon) after his first outing, “Hutch” (Bob Odenkirk) has been carrying out some dangerous tasks to try and reduce his $30 millions debt. After this most recent task, though, he declares that he is going to take an holiday with his wife (Connie Nielsen), his kids and his dad (Christopher Lloyd). They decide to return to one of his childhood haunts but aren’t there very long before “Hutch” sees red and is smashing up the people, the furniture, the fruit machines - even a duck-boat, and that earns his the attention of the menacingly ruthless “Lendina” (Sharon Stone) whose drug-smuggling enterprise is being interfered with, and she’s none too happy about that. When the pyrotechnics manage to destroy a fairly massive shipment of her cash and her “product” she is just going to have to come and settle the score herself - and that’s the denouement this builds to, quite entertainingly, for an hour and an half. The only thing it is missing is an alligator as noses and bones get broken left, right and centre; there is loads of betrayal and some new friendships made before the wonderfully hammy Stone and the underused Lloyd make their presence felt: the former more in the style of something from “John Wick”, the latter more from “The A-Team”. If their is a moral, well it’s probably never to give your arcade tickets to the girlfriend of the son of the local kingpin, otherwise maybe they’d just have eaten candy floss and gone home more rested.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
If I'm recalling George Orwell's 1984 correctly, one passage in the book talked about the blandness and general awfulness of the food offered by the authoritarian state. Cabbage that stank and coffee that wasn't real coffee. 

I have to say I've come to feel the same way about a lot of Western entertainment in recent years. It lacks vibrancy, individuality, it lacks flavour. 

The latest and I have to say  unwanted iteration of "Nobody", the unimaginatively  titled "Nobody 2" meets that definition. What made the first film work is precisely why the second film fails. It was a little original the first time around, with a reveal, that is, the suburban father being a talented assassin, no one had expected. With that out of the way whats left is anti climatic, repetitive  exposition, that's as uninspiring as its tired, 1970's theme park, setting. 

I know people starved for any kind of action film will like it. I get that. Speaking for myself personally, I'd like a little more. A dash of creativity, a spark of inspiration, not just more of the same beige entertainment, off the lazy Hollywood production line. 

In summary, "Nobody 2" is alright. Its a basic action flick that fills the entertainment gap but still leaves you craving something more substantial. A mediocre watch.

reviews.author: Chandler Danier
reviews.content:
Younger me would have really liked this. Maybe? Maybe I would have known that it was just rudderless action pasted back to back. It's pretty good but I already saw this with Christina Ricci. She was a better assassin.

Brother is definitely a welcome aspect of this. Never bring a machete to a katana fight is the best line in the film. I may not know because I skipped most of it. It's just a bunch of fighting. Some of it is quite inspired. Most of it is...well if you kill 100 people, can you kill all of them in novel ways? Unfortunately a little repetition seeps in.

1.5 hours. Well done. It only took me about 45 minutes to skip my way to pretty much knowing everything about this. Maybe it was 30 minutes. If you're a teen, you might like this. If you are an adult...you should be upset they didn't observe the laws of thermodynamics on the dart v knife portion of the evening. Satisfying, though. Nice to see the ladies stepping up. I'm still team Ricci, for my family kill time.

reviews.author: PeaceMeal
reviews.content:
Nobody (2021) was an outstanding film. Everything about it was innovative, surprising, funny, encouraging, etc. The believability factor was there too. I couldn't wait to watch Nobody 2 (2025).

Nobody 2 (2025) does what many successors do - but not all. It's a continuation with the story line but pumped up with totally outrageousness making it terribly unbelievable. It just became stupid to me. I was fine with never having seen #2. For me, the best part was the first 20-30 minutes. After that, it was just stupidness, but young gamers might like it.

I felt the same way after watching The Accountant 2.

Nobody (2021) = 8.5/10, but Nobody 2 (2025) = 6.5/10

reviews.author: Dr Nostromo
reviews.content:
79/100

After several assassin jobs to help pay off a debt, Hutch decides it's time to take his family on vacation and walks right into another mess. Much simpler and straight forward story line than the first film but the characters are just really fun to watch. That along with the humor, finely choreographed stunts and violent kills, my wife and I had a great time watching this one. Sharon Stone made a very different antagonist, perhaps a little over the top making her sort of ridiculous at times. But, overall, we're looking forward to future editions if they come about. -- DrNostromo.com

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Former assassin Hutch Mansell's peaceful family vacation devolves into chaos when a clash with a corrupt theme park operator pulls him back into a world of explosive violence.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Hutch Mansell attempts to leave his blood-soaked past behind by taking his family on a nostalgic getaway to a small-town theme park. However, trouble finds them when an encounter with a greedy park operator and a crooked local sheriff escalates into an all-out war. Forced to rely on his deadly skill set once again, Hutch must navigate corrupt authority figures and a ruthless crime boss. Ultimately, he must do whatever it takes to protect his loved ones and survive the bloody fallout.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Seeking a normal life, former government assassin Hutch Mansell decides to take his family on a quiet, nostalgic vacation to a quaint small-town theme park. What is supposed to be a harmless trip quickly sours after a confrontation with the park's corrupt operator. The situation worsens when the local crooked sheriff steps in, choosing to protect local criminal interests rather than enforce the law. As tensions boil over, Hutch finds himself targeted by a ruthless crime boss who controls the region's underworld. Unwilling to let his family become collateral damage, Hutch drops his mild-mannered persona and unleashes his full, lethal capabilities. He methodically dismantles the criminal network, utilizing everyday objects and tactical expertise to level the playing field. Along the way, his family is forced to reckon with the dangerous realities of Hutch's true nature as violence erupts around them. Fighting through waves of enforcers and corrupt officials, Hutch turns the theme park into a chaotic battleground. In the end, he ensures his family's safety by delivering brutal justice to everyone standing in their way.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: In this high-octane sequel, former government operative Hutch Mansell tries to trade bullet-riddled chaos for wholesome family bonding by bringing his family to a nostalgic small-town theme park. However, their peaceful holiday is shattered when a minor altercation with a corrupt park operator spirals out of control. Caught between a crooked sheriff enforcing local criminal rule and a ruthless crime lord pulling the strings from the shadows, Hutch is left with no choice but to reactivate his lethal skill set. Blending dark humor with relentless action, Hutch turns the tables on his adversaries to safeguard his family and clean up a corrupt town.

faq.answer: Yes, Nobody 2 is a direct sequel to the 2021 action-thriller film Nobody, expanding the franchise centered around former government assassin Hutch Mansell.
faq.question: Is Nobody 2 part of a franchise?

faq.answer: The dominant genre of Nobody 2 is action-thriller, featuring high-octane combat choreography, dark comedy elements, and intense suspense.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of Nobody 2?

faq.answer: Bob Odenkirk reprises his lead role as Hutch Mansell, the former deadly government 'auditor' trying to live a normal suburban life.
faq.question: Who plays the lead character in Nobody 2?

faq.answer: In Nobody 2, Hutch Mansell attempts to reconnect with his family during a vacation at a small-town theme park, but violence erupts when they clash with local corrupt operators and a ruthless crime syndicate.
faq.question: What is the main storyline of Nobody 2?

faq.answer: Nobody 2 was directed by acclaimed Indonesian filmmaker Timo Tjahjanto, known for his intense action and thriller films like The Night Comes for Us.
faq.question: Who directed Nobody 2?

faq.answer: Yes, original cast members Bob Odenkirk, Connie Nielsen (Becca), RZA (Harry), Christopher Lloyd (David), and Colin Salmon (The Barber) all return for the sequel.
faq.question: Are key cast members from the original film returning for Nobody 2?

faq.answer: The new antagonists include crime boss Lendina (played by Sharon Stone), a corrupt sheriff named Abel (played by Colin Hanks), and theme park operator Wyatt Martin (played by John Ortiz).
faq.question: Who are the new antagonists featured in Nobody 2?

faq.answer: While starting from the Mansell family's suburban life, the majority of the film takes place in Plummerville, Wisconsin, centered around a nostalgic small-town theme park and waterpark.
faq.question: Where does the primary action of Nobody 2 take place?

faq.answer: Yes, Nobody 2 includes a mid-credits/post-credits scene that hints at future complications and potential sequels for Hutch Mansell and his family.
faq.question: Is there a post-credits scene in Nobody 2?

faq.answer: Nobody 2 was produced by 87North Productions alongside Universal Pictures and Odenkirk Provissiero Entertainment.
